title: Easter Dates — the Computus, visualized
description: Western Easter for any year from 1583 to 4099 by the Anonymous Gregorian algorithm (Meeus/Jones/Butcher), with every intermediate variable shown. Orthodox Easter comes from the Julian computus and is converted to the Gregorian calendar through the Julian Day Number. A bar chart shows how often each date from March 22 to April 25 occurs over any range. Ash Wednesday, Palm Sunday, Good Friday, Ascension, Pentecost, Trinity Sunday and Corpus Christi are worked out from Easter.
prompt: Build an Easter date page using the Anonymous Gregorian algorithm (Meeus/Jones/Butcher). It should compute Western Easter for any year from 1583 to 4099 and show it step by step with the intermediate variables. Chart the distribution of Easter dates over a chosen range. The full 5,700,000-year cycle is too long, so do 1583–4099, and note that the earliest possible date is March 22 and the latest April 25. Derive the movable feasts from Easter: Ash Wednesday (−46), Palm Sunday, Pentecost (+49), Ascension (+39), Corpus Christi (+60). Also show Orthodox Easter via the Julian computus converted to Gregorian. Reference values for the spec: 2026-04-05 Western, 2026-04-12 Orthodox, 2025-04-20 for both, 2019-04-21, 2038-04-25, 2285-03-22.

methodology: Different-algorithm oracle: the spec implements Gauss's Easter algorithm, including its April 19 and April 18 exceptions, and checks the page's Meeus/Jones/Butcher result for all 2,517 years from 1583 to 4099. Every date must also be a Sunday.

Orthodox Easter is checked another way. The page converts the Julian date through the Julian Day Number, and the spec adds the century-rule gap ⌊Y/100⌋ − ⌊Y/400⌋ − 2 to the Julian date, for every year. Orthodox Easter must never come before Western Easter, and in 2100 the gap must go from 13 to 14 days.

Published reference dates: 2026 (April 5 Western, April 12 Orthodox, Julian March 30), 2025 (April 20 for both, with the 'same Sunday' message), 2019 (April 21 and April 28), 2038 (April 25) and 2285 and 1818 (March 22). For 2026 each intermediate variable a…m is checked against the spec's own step-by-step calculation.

Distribution: over 1583–4099 there must be exactly 35 bars, from March 22 to April 25, holding 2,517 years. Each bar's count must equal the Gauss oracle's, and the most common date must match. For 2000–2099 the counts are recomputed and March 22 must be 0. A backwards range is refused.

Feasts are checked against day offsets from Easter that the test computes itself, and against the published 2026 calendar (Ash Wednesday Feb 18, Ascension May 14, Pentecost May 24, Corpus Christi Jun 4). page.clock sets 'this year' to 2027 to check the default year and the This year button.
risks: Integer division and mod: JavaScript's % is a remainder, so a negative intermediate value would be silently wrong. All the Meeus terms stay non-negative in 1583–4099, and the full-range sweep would show any failure.
Julian → Gregorian conversion around a centurial year, where the gap between the calendars grows by a day. The JDN route and the spec's gap formula have to agree in 1700, 1800, 1900 and 2100.
Date objects and time zones: every date is built with Date.UTC and read with UTC getters, so a test machine in a far-west time zone doesn't move Easter to Saturday.
Corpus Christi is +60 (Thursday), but many dioceses now keep it on the following Sunday. The page says so rather than choosing one silently.
qa.playwright: The two whole-range tests make one page.evaluate call each, which returns 2,517 results that the spec compares with its own algorithm in Node. The first version called expect() about 10,000 times inside the loop, and on a busy machine the Orthodox test went past the 30-second timeout even though every value was right. Collecting mismatches into an array and asserting it once made it fast, and the failure message is clearer too. Chart bars carry data-count attributes, so the distribution is read with evaluateAll instead of from pixels. page.clock.install only pins 'now' for the default-year test; the page has no animation to drive.
coverage: Intermediate variables for 2026 (Gregorian and Julian, +13 days)
All years 1583–4099 vs Gauss; Orthodox vs century-gap formula; Sundays; 2100 gap of 14
Distribution: 35 bars, counts, earliest/latest/mode, sub-range, bad range, Orthodox toggle
Movable feasts for 2026; clock-driven default year; year limits and error message

a11y: The year field is a labelled number input whose error message sits in an alert region, and the previous and next buttons have text labels. The Western and Orthodox dates update in an aria-live region. The step tables use row headers. The chart's aria-label gives the range, the earliest, latest and most common date, and the full counts are also in a table inside a details element. The Western/Orthodox choice is a pair of toggle buttons.
